index.title: Product Factory Strategist — AI agent for product directors
index.description: An AI agent: from a vague request to an evidence-based strategy — claims registry, red team, Excel models and a committee six-pager.
index.k009: AI agent · evidence-based strategy · human in the loop
index.k010: From a vague request to an evidence-based strategy you can trust
index.k011: The agent runs real research: a plan built from decision-changing questions, verifiable sources, a claim registry, substantively distinct options and a red-team attack, product & communication strategies, a validation plan — and Excel models attached to a six-pager for the committee. After the decision, it tracks commitments and revisits conclusions on new data.
index.k026: The competition's required minimum is fully covered, plus advanced capabilities. Every number has a type (fact/hypothesis/forecast/assumption/inference), strength A–D, and a source S###.
index.k029: Clarifies question, goal, audience, constraints, data. Asks only what matters next. A human approves the brief.
index.k031: Websites, PDF, DOCX, XLSX, CSV, images — from allowed domains. Deduped by URL and SHA-256, prompt-injection scanner.
index.k033: The plan starts from decision-changing questions. A fact without a source cannot be stored; synthetic respondents yield hypotheses only.
index.k036: ≥3 substantively distinct options, including "do nothing" and "shut down". A dedicated subagent attacks each one.
index.k039: Audience, trade-offs, economics; barrier, message, channels. The "promise → proof" table is verified automatically.
index.k041: FAQ-1…FAQ-6 report + four formula-driven workbooks: unit economics, growth, cohorts, market sizing. Built in background, recalculated on open.
index.k044: Grounds, owners, commitments, review dates. "What to decide now", stale grounds, impact of new data.
index.k047: Action log, grounds behind each conclusion, cost in tokens and money. Every step is visible and reproducible.
index.k050: The agent drives the work and calls the human only for a consequential choice. Progress shows as: Step N/12 · research · sources S001–S009 · next: situation. Double Diamond phases: Discover (0–3) → Define (4–6) → Develop (7–9) → Deliver (10–12).
index.k075: Work can be interrupted and resumed in a new chat or another environment: all state lives in project files. Finished steps are never repeated.
index.k077: Demo: CVStart — from the director's task to a six-pager
index.k078: An end-to-end run on a live open-source product — cvstart.org: an AI resume builder + job search, 129 job boards scanned, 19 languages. Below: the product screenshot, the detailed brief and task plan, the agent's algorithm, its conclusion and validation thresholds. Full walkthrough on a separate page.
index.k080: The demo's product: cvstart.org — an open-source (MIT) AI resume builder and job-search dashboard. 100% local, 18 BYOK LLM providers.
index.k082: Product: CVStart (career-ops UI) — an open-source (MIT) AI resume builder and job-search dashboard: ~129 job boards scanned (124 EN + 5 RU: hh.ru, Habr Career, etc.), AI fit-scoring 0.0–5.0 against the user's resume, CV Studio (JD tuning, humanize, ATS bullets), PDF/DOCX export, cover letters, an auto pipeline, an application tracker with follow-up, a job map, mock interviews. 100% local — data stays with the user; 18 BYOK LLM providers + keyless; 19 UI languages; ~7,602 automated tests. No monetization: "$0 forever", no public hosting [S001][S002].
index.k083: The task (verbatim): "Design the commercial version of cvstart.org — resume building, job search — and a go-to-market strategy for the whole world." Comparison axis: paying-subscriber and ARR growth. Constraints (director's intake answers): the open-source core stays MIT · a solo developer · preserving the trust of the local-first mode.
index.k084: Task plan — the agent's 12 steps: 0 · brief: decision, comparison axis, constraints → 00_brief.md — pause: the director approves 1–2 · sources & research: the product's site and README, 4 market digests with URLs, a synthetic funnel → {{S_RANGE}}, {{C_RANGE}}, 01_research_plan.md 3–4 · discovery & situation: 2 AI personas (hypotheses, not facts), knowns / unknowns / tensions → 02_situation.md 5 · five options A–E + a red-team attack: 15 objections + 5 hidden assumptions → 03_options.md 6 · the director's choice: option B — hosted freemium SaaS — pause 7–8 · strategies & validation plan: 04/05 + 06 (thresholds at week {{FUNNEL_WEEKS}}) 9 · quality review: check --strict 100/100 10 · decision D001: commitment and review — pause 11 · monitoring: commitments and re-examinations, pfs decision due
index.k103: Option B — hosted freemium SaaS, global: Free (BYOK — zero cost) / Pro $12 / Unlimited $29 tiers; opt-in cloud on top of the local MIT core; honest no-auto-renewal pricing as positioning; language waves EN → DE/ES/PT-BR → JA/ZH from 19 ready locales. Launch channels: Product Hunt, Hacker News, "open-source Jobscan alternative" SEO.
index.k104: Conscious trade-offs: no B2B white-label (C) — a solo founder lacks the sales motion; no dual-license (D) — legally impossible on top of MIT; no shutdown (E) — abandoning an asset in a growing market ({{MARKET}}, AI CAGR {{AI_CAGR}}).
index.k106: Decision {{DECISION_ID}}: grounds C019/C013/C014/C016/C005/C006 · commitment "hosted beta in 3 EN geos by {{COMMIT_DATE}}" · review {{REVIEW_DATE}} · stop trigger: paid < {{PAID_LOW}} with activation < {{ACT_STOP}}% → option E.
index.k107: Thresholds ({{BETA_WEEKS}}-week beta): continue — paid ≥ {{PAID_TARGET}}, activation ≥ {{ACT_TARGET}}%, churn ≤ {{CHURN_MAX}}% → DE/ES/PT-BR wave · change — paid {{PAID_LOW}}–{{PAID_HIGH}} → rebuild tiers/pricing · stop — paid < {{PAID_LOW}} with activation < {{ACT_STOP}}% → the project stays OSS.
index.k108: Counter-metrics: GitHub stars (drop < 30%), GDPR complaints, free-tier inference ≤ $200/mo, NPS ≥ 30.
index.k119: The committee six-pager: what exactly the agent collects
index.k120: A six-pager is six committee questions, six evidence-backed answers. Below is the detailed anatomy: what data the agent collects into each section, from which workflow steps, and how each section is quality-checked.
index.k121: The anatomy of FAQ-1…6: data → workflow step → quality gate
index.k122: FAQ-1 · Current state analysis1.1 Market overview — volume and dynamics as ranges, a year-by-year forecast in bullets, key trends with bold headlines and product implications. 1.2 Competitors — a table of "advantages / growth strategies and promo mechanics / risks for us" rated High–Medium–Low. Gate: every number is a C###/S### tag; diverging estimates become ranges; source footnotes with URLs at the bottom.
index.k123: FAQ-2 · User Persona: who is the target audience2.1 Segments — a table with fixed rows "Who they are / What they use today and why / What difficulties they face / Common difficulties" plus prioritization reasoning with math. 2.2 Journey barriers — a "stage → barrier → what the product does" table and per-segment "what blocks start/renewal". Synthetic data — flagged as hypotheses.
index.k124: FAQ-3 · Strategic initiative-driversAn intro — which option the direction was chosen from (a reference to the options analysis and the red team). Then 3–4 initiatives with numbered subsections, the "First driver — … / Second driver — …" construction, "Key directions" bullets and a step-by-step unit-economics calculation (formula → substitution → result). Closed with an inference conclusion.
index.k125: FAQ-4 · TacticsThe matrix "Strategic initiative | Focus | User needs & desires | Solutions (tactics)": 2–4 rows per initiative; tactics are executable (what exactly gets built), not slogans; needs cover both the user and the operator where relevant. Every tactic is backed by a FAQ-1–3 conclusion.
index.k126: FAQ-5 · High-level implementation planThe expected initiative contribution split — as percentages (summing to 100%) with weight reasoning; tactic order "high → medium → basic" priority; timing tied to market seasons (the launch meets the January hiring peak); parallel tracks; decision D001 with a commitment, a review and a stop trigger.
index.k127: FAQ-6 · Success metricsKPIs in two planes: 1) Business — revenue/paying users/conversion/tier share/actual LTV-CAC; 2) Product — activation, time-to-first-value, fewer actions, churn, NPS. Each has a baseline, a deadline target and an action threshold; at the bottom — source footnotes S### with URLs, as in the reference.
index.k128: Formats: for the committee in any language
index.k129: The six-pager is assembled in two language versions — RU and EN — and three formats each: Markdown (the tagged evidence registry), PDF (print A4 layout: typography, tables, formulas) and DOCX (Word — no third-party packages). Screenshots are deliberately excluded: a committee document is verifiable reasoning, conclusions and calculations, not pictures. The assembly method — knowledge/templates/SIX_PAGER_PROMPT.md.
index.k131: unit_economics — contribution, LTV/CAC, payback, sensitivity to ARPU / variable costs / CAC / churn · growth_model — 12 months: input → orders → revenue → margin · cohort_retention — cohorts, retention curve, M1/M3/M6 · market_sizing — PAM→TAM→SAM→SOM and environment factors. Workbooks are built from the project by one command; recalculation happens on open in Excel / Numbers / LibreOffice.
index.k134: The agent's layers: environment (AGENTS.md, 121 skills, 8 subagents, 4 hooks) → the tools/pfs CLI+MCP core → a knowledge base of 89 method cards and integrations. Guarantees live in pfs code, not in prompts; state lives in project files, so work survives breaks and moves between environments.
index.k150: Guarantees live in pfs code, not in prompts
index.k154: You need Python 3.9+ and any environment: Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, Windsurf, Copilot. No packages to install.
index.k155: $ git clone https://github.com/Fighter90/product-factory-strategist.git $ cd product-factory-strategist $ python3 -m tools.pfs doctor # environment check ✓ Python 3.12: ok · pdftotext: present · knowledge-base cards: 89 $ python3 -m unittest discover -s tests ✓ Ran 115 tests — OK
index.k156: The agent creates the project, asks 1–3 questions, runs the research and shows progress. Say "stop" to pause, "clarify: …" to adjust, "build the six-pager" for the committee report. After a break, open a new chat — state is restored automatically.
index.k159: The agent runs most actions itself — commands are for oversight and manual operations.
index.k160: GroupCommandsPurpose Projectsnew · list · use · statuscreate/select a project, resume point Stepsstep · next · questions <step>step mark + mandatory cards; "what to decide now"; question blocks Sourcessource add/list/show · source refresh S###websites, PDF, DOCX, XLSX → S###, deduped and protected Claimsclaim add/list/supersede/retract/rebaseC### registry: fact/hypothesis/forecast/assumption/inference, grade A–D Qualitycheck --strict · impactuntagged numbers, dead links; what a change affects Decisionsdecision add/due/done/rebasegrounds, owners, commitments, revisions Datadata profile/cohort/funnel/statstable profile, cohorts, funnel, stats with 95% CI Excel & reportscalc · export [--six-pager|--deck] · docxformula workbooks; REPORT; six-pager; HTML deck; Word Knowledge & modelskb search/show/index · modelssearch across 89 cards; models per task Costcost · log --usdtokens and money per task
index.k163: What is "Product Factory Strategist"?An AI agent — a folder of instructions, a knowledge base of 89 method cards and CLI/MCP tools (pfs). It walks a product director from a vague request to an evidence-based product & communication strategy with a validation plan — and keeps working after the decision.
index.k164: How is it different from a plain AI chat?Every material statement carries a source (S###), a type (fact/hypothesis/forecast/assumption/inference) and a grade A–D. In the demo run 100% of numbers trace to sources; a plain chat scores 0%. Plus: options attacked by red team, a validation plan, and a decision with grounds and an audit log.
index.k165: Are my data and sources safe?Public sources and your own materials only. Secrets live in .env, never in the repo. Commands found inside sources are never executed — flagged as injection attempts. Allowed domains are checked before any fetch.
index.k166: Can I move a project to another environment?Yes. A project is a plain folder (projects/<slug>/): copy it or git push/pull and open in Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, Windsurf or Copilot. pfs status restores the context.
index.k167: What happens after the decision?The decision is recorded as D###: grounds (C###), owner, metric, review date, commitments. pfs decision due surfaces what to decide now; pfs impact shows which conclusions new data affects; pfs claim supersede updates stale claims without losing history.
index.k170: Full documentation lives on a dedicated page: talking to the agent, process steps, Excel models, environments, security, skills and troubleshooting — with in-page search.
index.k172: Control phrases: "stop", "clarify: …", "what should I decide now".
index.k175: What happens at each of the 12 steps and who decides.
index.k181: Symptom → fix: sources, domains, Excel, environments.

help.title: Help — Product Factory Strategist
help.description: Full documentation for the Product Factory Strategist AI agent: the 12 process steps, sources S###, claims C###, decisions D###, Excel models, the six-pager, skills, subagents, MCP, environments, security and troubleshooting.
help.k009: Full documentation: talking to the agent, all 12 process steps, evidence S### → C### → D###, Excel models and the six-pager, tooling (CLI, MCP, skills, subagents, hooks), environments and integrations, security, glossary and troubleshooting.
help.k010: 12 steps · 89 knowledge cards · 121 skills · 8 subagents · 4 hooks · 18 MCP tools · 0 dependencies
help.k071: Key points — the whole gist in one minute
help.k073: Every number and conclusion: a type (fact/hypothesis/forecast/assumption/inference), grade A–D, and a source. The chain S### → C### → D### is traceable from link to decision.
help.k075: The agent drives: brief → sources → research → discovery → situation → options → choice → strategies → validation → review → decision → monitoring.
help.k077: At least three substantively distinct ones, including "do nothing" and "shut it down". A dedicated red-team subagent attacks each.
help.k079: projects/<slug>/ stores everything. New chat, another environment, a break — work resumes where it stopped, no repeats.
help.k081: 4 workbooks (unit economics, growth, cohorts, market) build in the background; the Input sheet holds parameters, the rest are formulas.
help.k083: An action log, grounds behind conclusions, cost in tokens and money — pfs cost, pfs next, pfs check --strict.
help.k085: Write in plain language as to a colleague. The agent understands three kinds of messages: a task ("why is in-app retention dropping"), answers to its questions (pick an option or reply freely) and control phrases (see below). It never asks more than three questions at once and always explains what it is missing and why it matters for the next step.
help.k086: A good first request names the decision to make: "Help me decide whether to launch antispam as a paid subscription; here is the brief and six months of data." A weak one ("make me a strategy") also works — the agent clarifies the decision, audience and constraints via pfs ask before spending your tokens.
help.k088: PhraseWhat happens "stop"Pause: state saved, the agent stays quiet until a new command "clarify: …"Adjust the task; only the affected part is redone, sources are not duplicated "redo section X"Targeted rework of a single document section "what should I decide now"pfs next: current step, overdue decisions, stale grounds, open questions "what's due"pfs decision due: decisions and commitments whose review date arrived "what will this new source affect"pfs impact: which conclusions, document lines and decisions go stale "build the six-pager"pfs calc all + pfs export --six-pager: FAQ-1…6 report and 4 Excel workbooks "recalculate Excel"pfs calc all — workbooks rebuilt from current calcs.json "build the report" / "build the deck"pfs export → REPORT.md; pfs export --deck → 16:9 HTML deck "make it a doc"pfs docx file.md — Markdown to Word, dependency-free "check the project"pfs check --strict — numbers, links, options "how much did it cost"pfs cost — tokens and money per model
help.k090: $ git clone https://github.com/Fighter90/product-factory-strategist.git $ cd product-factory-strategist $ python3 -m tools.pfs doctor # environment check $ python3 -m unittest discover -s tests # 115 tests, optional $ pfs new "Why is retention dropping" "the request verbatim"
help.k091: Requirements: Python 3.9+ and any supported environment. No packages to install — standard library only. Secrets (Linear and other MCP keys) go to .env — it is git-ignored and not required for the basic loop.
help.k093: pfs new "<name>" "<the request verbatim>" creates projects/<slug>/ (sources, interviews, analysis, outputs, state.json, log.jsonl) and activates it. The agent then: classifies the scenario via routing (pfs route), asks the intake question block — up to 3 questions — writes outputs/00_brief.md and stops for your approval. That is the first of three human pauses.
help.k094: Switch projects with pfs use <slug>, list them with pfs list, inspect state with pfs status.
help.k095: CVStart demo: how it was made and what to look at
help.k096: A full end-to-end run on a live open-source product — cvstart.org (AI resume builder + job search: 129 job boards, AI scoring, 19 languages): 12 steps, 5 options, 20 red-team objections, both strategies, a six-pager in 6 formats (RU/EN × MD/PDF/DOCX, each with its language's screenshots), 4 Excel workbooks, decision D001, check --strict 100/100. Project: projects/демо/; interactive walkthrough: demo.html.
help.k097: What to look at (in order): 00_brief → 01_research_plan → 02_situation → 03_options (5 options + 20 red-team objections) → 04/05 (strategies) → 06_validation_plan (90-day thresholds) → REPORT.md and SIX_PAGER_RU / SIX_PAGER_EN in .md/.pdf/.docx; Excel in outputs/attachments/; product screenshots in outputs/img/ (19 locales); the action log is log.jsonl.
help.k098: Mistakes along the way (honestly): market estimates from aggregators diverge ×2 — recorded as ranges [S006]; source numbering shifted during re-registration — tags re-bound and re-checked with check --strict; some C### links drifted to neighbouring claims during migration — caught by a registry audit and fixed. The human helped at three pauses: brief, option choice, decision D001 approval.
help.k100: The cycle is 12 steps in four double-diamond phases: Discover (0–3) → Define (4–6) → Develop (7–9) → Deliver (10–11). Each step has mandatory knowledge cards (pfs step prints them), a question block (pfs questions <step>), quality gates and an artifact. Progress shows in one line: Step N/12 · research · sources S001–S009 · next: situation. Steps 0, 6, 10 are human pauses: brief, option choice, decision approval.
help.k103: Input: your request verbatim. Agent: clarifies the target decision, goal, audience and format, constraints, available data — the intake question block (≤3 questions with options and a recommendation). Output: outputs/00_brief.md. Human: approves the brief — it is then fixed and can ground assumptions (like source S011 in the demo). Commands: pfs new, pfs questions intake, pfs answer "…".
help.k106: Input: your files and a list of public pages. Agent: registers materials — pfs source add <url|file> — dedup by URL and SHA-256 (a repeat adds nothing), extracts text from PDF/DOCX/XLSX/CSV/pages, checks the domain against the project's allowed_sources, flags embedded instruction-like phrases (data, not commands). Output: sources/S###.md + copies in sources/raw/. Commands: add/list/show/refresh; refreshing a web source compares hashes and warns on changes.
help.k109: Agent: builds a plan from questions that could change the decision ("question → if yes / if no → how it affects"), extracts claims with type, grade and quote, runs calculations, prepares interviews when needed. A fact without a source cannot be stored — the tool refuses. Output: outputs/01_research_plan.md, claims.jsonl (C###), analysis/. Commands: pfs claim add, pfs data profile|cohort|funnel|stats, pfs interview guide|save, pfs media add. Gate: every key question answered with a C### or an explicitly named gap.
help.k112: Agent: builds personas and their jobs-to-be-done, describes user alternatives — how people solve the problem today; the discovery question block fixes the segment. AI respondents (the synthetic-respondent subagent) yield hypotheses about motives and barriers — registered with origin=synthetic and unable to prove demand. Output: the "Segments" section of 02_situation.md, transcripts in interviews/synthetic/.
help.k115: Agent: assembles a verifiable picture: what is known and from where (C### tags), what we do not know and why it matters, contradictions between sources. Every number in a document must carry a tag — check catches "naked" numbers. Output: outputs/02_situation.md. Gate: pfs check with zero errors.
help.k118: Agent: prepares at least three substantively distinct options, including "do nothing" and "shut it down" — check verifies their presence by keywords. Each with: strong objections (attacked by the red-team subagent), formula-based economics with ranges, and the conditions under which the option is right. Output: outputs/03_options.md. Gate: red team has responded, check passes.
help.k121: Agent: shows the option comparison (criteria, economics, risks) and a single recommendation, then asks — pfs ask "Which option do we take?" --options "A,B,C". Human: picks the option — the answer is stored in state.json and grounds the strategies and the D### decision (like S011 in the CVStart demo). No strategies are written before the choice.
help.k124: Agent: writes the product strategy — audience and their job, alternatives, the chosen direction and conscious trade-offs, benefit-to-cost economics — and the communication strategy — audience and situation, the comprehension barrier, the key message, its proof, channel roles. Consistency is enforced by a "promise → product proof" table: every promise cites a C###. The comms-strategist subagent drafts the comms part. Output: 04_product_strategy.md, 05_comms_strategy.md.
help.k127: Agent: states the expected change (which metric, by how much), the comparison baseline (prior period, control group), the observation window, unwanted side effects (counter-metrics), and continue / adjust / stop criteria. All five sections are mandatory — check enforces them. Output: outputs/06_validation_plan.md.
help.k130: Agent: runs pfs check --strict, requests an independent rubric review (the evidence-auditor subagent) and assembles the committee pack: pfs calc all (4 Excel workbooks) and pfs export --six-pager (FAQ-1…6 + attachments). On a borderline score the model escalates and the step repeats. Output: outputs/07_quality_review.md, SIX_PAGER.md, attachments/*.xlsx.
help.k133: Agent: records the decision via pfs decision add: title, statement, owner, grounds (C###), metric with target and date, review date, trigger ("if X — revisit"), commitments ("what | who | when"). Human: approves the decision. Output: a record in decisions.jsonl (D###). From now on pfs next and pfs decision due watch the deadlines.
help.k136: Agent: keeps the step open: pfs decision due lists overdue reviews; when new data arrives — pfs source refresh + pfs impact C### locate affected conclusions; stale ones are superseded via pfs claim supersede, conclusions redirected by pfs claim rebase, decisions by pfs decision rebase. Gate: pfs decision due is empty or fully handled.
help.k138: A source is the minimal unit of trust. pfs source add <url> downloads the page and extracts text; pfs source add <file> accepts PDF, DOCX, XLSX, CSV, images (your description of what is visible). For a JS-rendered page: save the text manually and add pfs source add --text-file saved.md --url <url> --title "…". For screenshots/audio descriptions: pfs media add (see Media & UX).
help.k139: Hygiene: dedup by URL and SHA-256; the domain is checked against projects/<slug>/project.json → allowed_sources (a hook blocks foreign domains before the request); pfs source list — the registry, pfs source show S### — text and metadata; pfs source refresh S### — reload: hash changed → warning and a reminder to run pfs impact S###.
help.k140: Source types: public, own, interview, synthetic
help.k141: OriginWhat it isConstraint public/webPublic pages and publications (default)Project-allowed domains ownYour materials: briefs, data dumps, internal docsNo closed or personal data interviewReal interviews — with participant consentNo personal data in the repository syntheticAI respondents, model-generated dataHypotheses only: facts on synthetic data are blocked by the checker
help.k143: A claim is the atom of knowledge. The registry is claims.jsonl; written only via pfs claim add:
help.k144: TypeWhen to useRequirement factA verified statementSource required; never on synthetic data; grade D forbidden hypothesisAn assumption we intend to testGrounds: a source or other claims forecastA model-based predictionGrounds + visible assumptions in the model assumptionAccepted without testing (demo frame, model scenario)Grounds: where it came from (checker warns otherwise) inferenceYour conclusion from other claims--from required; never stronger than its weakest input
help.k146: An inference is never stronger than its weakest critical input: two C grounds and one B give at most C. Set via claim add --grade; supersede preserves the grade automatically.
help.k147: Supersede, retract, rebase — history is kept
help.k148: After supersede, documents referencing the old ID get a check error with the replacement hint (replacement: C058) — re-tag the lines and rebuild exports. This is a guard, not a bug: documents cannot silently rely on stale claims. The history (who, when, why) stays in the registry.
help.k150: pfs impact C005 / pfs impact S002 shows transitively: which claims rely on it, which document lines cite it, which decisions are grounded in it. Practice: impact before an edit, impact after, then pfs check --strict as the final filter.
help.k152: Track: pfs decision due — overdue items, due reviews, decisions with stale grounds; pfs decision done --id D001 --commitment K1 — close a commitment; pfs decision list — registry. New data changed the grounds? — run impact, supersede, then pfs decision rebase --id D001 --note "…".
help.k154: REPORT.md — the final document with all attachments
help.k155: pfs export assembles REPORT.md: summary, brief, situation, options and choice, both strategies, the validation plan, appendices (claim registry with grades and sources, cost log, Excel links). Edit only outputs/*.md by hand — REPORT rebuilds so nothing drifts. pfs export --six-pager — the committee format.
help.k158: The file is projects/<slug>/calcs.json. The agent fills values from claims and records grounds in note; missing keys fall back to examples marked "EXAMPLE", visible in Excel.
help.k160: pfs calc all|unit-econ|growth|cohort|market writes workbooks to outputs/attachments/. The Input sheet holds editable parameters (with source notes); all other sheets are live formulas: CM, LTV, LTV/CAC, payback, sensitivity (unit economics); MAU → orders → GMV → margin over 12 months (growth); cohorts and M1–M12 retention; PAM→TAM→SAM→SOM.
help.k161: Editing: change the Input values — Excel recalculates. If you edit calcs.json — rerun pfs calc all and pfs export --six-pager so the text and workbooks match. A file preview may look "empty" — that is a cached render; formulas compute on open.
help.k163: pfs export --deck builds a 16:9 HTML deck from SIX_PAGER.md — section slides in the site's gradient theme, printable to PDF from the browser. pfs docx <file.md> converts Markdown to Word (headings, tables, lists, inline code), dependency-free — for handing documents to the committee.
help.k166: The pfs-strategist server (stdio, stdlib only) plugs into any environment's .mcp.json — the agent gets the same operations as the CLI. Tools:
help.k167: Skills (120): structure and three ways to invoke
help.k168: Structure: base per-step skills (13) · product-skills, method procedures (27) · a personal library of ~59 (design, marketing, science, documents & media, thinking modes, meta) · integrations. Each folder .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md holds instructions + scripts + references.
help.k169: Invocation: 1) automatic — description triggers; 2) explicit — "use skill <name>: <task>"; 3) per step — pfs step prints mandatory cards. Priority rule: project methodology (KB maps) outranks generic skills. Integration examples: hallmark (anti-slop page gates), board-of-directors (5-perspective council + Red Team at options), premortem (failure pre-mortem before approval), rea (reverse-engineering JS pages and closed formats), sdd (development discipline), deck (six-pager presentation), deep-research (literature review via Feynman). Full registry: docs/SKILLS.md.
help.k173: The model profile lives in config/models.json: cheap models for classification, extraction, rubric scoring, AI respondents; strong ones for synthesis, options, red team, strategy. pfs models — table; pick — per task; use — switch profile; pfs route --economy downgrades deep→balanced except red team. Escalation: two consecutive check failures or a borderline rubric score → pfs models escalate <task> and retry with a stronger model. Subagents inherit the profile; pfs models sync after changes.
help.k175: The Stop hook recomputes cost from the session transcript (prices from config/pricing.json); pfs cost — totals per model and task; pfs cost --window — periods. Human edits count too: pfs log "brief edit" --human-minutes 15. Demo reference: a full project ≈ $19 with a mixed model profile.
help.k176: Data analysis: profile, cohort, funnel, stats
help.k177: Before computing, the agent checks metrics, units, periods and gaps (table profile). --save makes a run reproducible. Results go to analysis/ and are anchored as C### claims with the file as source.
help.k179: pfs interview guide --persona "Parent, kids 7–12" builds the guide; pfs interview save transcript.md registers it with origin=synthetic. The synthetic-respondent subagent plays the persona. Honesty rule: synthetic answers yield hypotheses only; the checker refuses facts on them; documents mark them as model-generated. Real interviews require consent and no personal data.
help.k181: pfs media add shot.png --desc "what is visible" --title "…" copies the media to sources/raw/ and turns the description into a text source: the agent analyzes exactly what is described. pfs ux scaffold S003 --focus "onboarding" builds a heuristics + journey scaffold bound to the material; the ux-analyst subagent fills it without inventing beyond the screenshots.
help.k182: Environment: Claude Code — the full experience
help.k183: Open the repo folder in Claude Code — everything auto-loads: 121 skills, 8 subagents, 4 hooks, the CLI (pfs …) and MCP tools. Just state the task — the agent takes it from there.
help.k184: Environments: Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, Windsurf, Copilot
help.k185: All environments read AGENTS.md. Cursor — .cursor/rules + MCP from .mcp.json. Codex / OpenCode / Windsurf / Copilot — no hooks: start with "read AGENTS.md and run pfs status" — the agent restores context and continues. The pfs-strategist MCP works everywhere (path-independent launcher).
help.k187: MCP server npx mcp-server-linear, key LINEAR_API_KEY in .env (git-ignored). The agent reads issues, comments progress, closes with reports — as in this project: PRO-5…PRO-24 closed with final comments. Same rule: the human decides — no issues are closed without your word.
help.k189: MCP https://mcp.lovable.dev is wired in .mcp.json; authorize once via OAuth (/mcp → lovable → Authenticate). Then the agent creates and edits Lovable projects on request: this project's landing lives in the repo (canonical) and in Lovable (mirror). create_project/send_message consume Lovable credits; ready prompts are in docs/lovable-brief.md.
help.k191: Higgsfield — image/video generation (this page's art is its work). REA — reverse-engineering of JS pages and closed formats (HAR, SQLite, APK) when plain fetch returns nothing. Feynman — deep-research CLI (literature reviews); a search-provider key is needed for live runs. officecli — Office documents in/out. All are optional MCP/CLI add-ons to the basic loop.
help.k193: All state lives in projects/<slug>/: state.json (steps, choices, questions), claims.jsonl, decisions.jsonl, log.jsonl, sources/, outputs/. New chat in the repo folder: the SessionStart hook feeds status and "what to decide now" automatically. Hook-less environment: write "read AGENTS.md and run pfs status". Finished steps never repeat; sources and claims never duplicate.
help.k195: A project is a plain folder: copy projects/<slug>/ (or git push/pull if tracked) and open elsewhere. The only non-portable part is secrets in .env: move them manually, never commit. The model profile (config/models.json) is repo-wide.
help.k197: Data: public sources and your materials only; no closed company data, no respondents' personal data. Domains: allow-listed in project.json; a hook blocks foreign domains pre-request. Secrets: .env only, git-ignored; no keys ever committed. Embedded instructions: source texts are data; "ignore instructions" inside a source is flagged, never executed. Interviews: real ones need consent; no personal data in the repo; synthetic data is honestly labeled.

materials.description: CVStart demo project materials: the committee six-pager in RU/EN (MD · PDF · DOCX), four Excel models, cvstart.org screenshots and the evidence base — sources S001–S002, S004–S011 (S003 merged into S006), claims C001–C020, decision D001.
materials.k007: Demo project materials: the committee six-pager in two languages and three formats, four Excel models with live formulas, product screenshots and a complete evidence base. Everything lives in the repository: projects/демо/.
materials.k015: The run's final report in the FAQ-1…6 strategic-reference structure: market and product state, segments and personas, 5 options with red team, hosted-freemium tactics, the beta plan and metrics. Assembled with the pfs export --six-pager command; each language comes in three formats.
materials.k017: The state of the resume-builder market, segment and persona hypotheses, 5 options A–E with 20 red-team hits, Free / Pro $12 / Unlimited $29 tactics, a hosted-beta plan for 3 EN geos, and decision thresholds.
materials.k018: RU · MD · PDF · DOCX · every number traces to C001–C020
materials.k021: The state of the resume-builder market, segments and persona hypotheses, 5 options A–E with 20 red-team hits, Free / Pro {{PRO_PRICE}} / Unlimited {{UNLIMITED_PRICE}} tactics, the {{BETA_WEEKS}}-week hosted-beta plan ({{COMMIT_DATE}} → {{REVIEW_DATE}}) and decision thresholds.
materials.k022: EN · MD · PDF · DOCX · every number traces to C001–C020
materials.k024: Plus SIX_PAGER.md — a draft the agent assembles itself with the pfs export --six-pager command, in the growth-strategy reference format (numbered subsections 1.1/1.2 and 2.1/2.2, an "Initiative | Focus | Needs | Solutions" tactics matrix, KPIs in two planes, auto footnotes from sources): open it in the repository. The draft's level of detail follows the prompt spec in knowledge/templates/SIX_PAGER_PROMPT.md.
materials.k025: One source — three formats: MD for reading and editing, PDF for the committee, DOCX for the director's edits. The content matches character-for-character within the registry's numbers.
materials.k027: Four workbooks in outputs/attachments/: editable inputs on the "Input" sheet — formulas recalculate on open, assumptions change on the fly. Every Input value traces to a claim C###; the demo's unit assumptions are [C016].
materials.k028: Per-paying-user contribution (CM $21.75), LTV ≈ $271.88, LTV/CAC ≈ 4.5, CAC payback ≈ 2.8 months, sensitivity to price and churn.
materials.k031: A 12-month growth model: the funnel visits → signups → activations → paying users → MRR; cross-checked against the beta expectation (model: 53 paying users by week 12 [S008]).
materials.k034: Beta signup cohorts, retention and activation curves by week; churn ≤ 10% — the "continue" threshold.
materials.k037: PAM→TAM→SAM→SOM of the resume-builder market ($1.2–2.4B [C005]) and the go-to-market PESTEL factors.
materials.k041: The demo's live product — cvstart.org: a landing page in two locales, a job-search dashboard with AI scoring, a job map and an application tracker.
materials.k043: The landing page in the Russian locale: "$0 forever", a scan of ~129 job boards (124 EN + 5 RU), 19 languages [S001].
materials.k045: The landing page's English locale — the starting point of the EN wave in the go-to-market strategy.
materials.k047: The job-search dashboard: AI job scoring 0.0–5.0 against the resume — the product's core.
materials.k049: The English dashboard: fit scoring against the resume — what users compare with Jobscan and Teal.
materials.k051: The job map on top of the ~129-job-board scan — the geography of offers.
materials.k053: The application tracker with follow-up — the response funnel between search sessions, the retention base of the hosted version.
materials.k054: Full UI versions exist in all 19 locales — the screenshots live in the career-ops-ui → images/ repository folder.
materials.k056: Every material is registered as a source (S###); claims with a type and evidence strength (C###) are extracted from them; options, strategies and decision D001 are built on those claims — the chain is traceable from a link to the decision.
materials.k069: The final report: sources S001–S011 except S003 (merged into S006), claims C001–C020 with type and A–D strength, decision D001 with grounds and commitments, metrics and the supersession history.
materials.k072: 10 sources with preserved text: Wiseguy Reports (resume-builder market size), Rezi Pricing (competitor prices), Kickresume Press (AI trends), SkyQuest (online recruiting, ATS) — plus the product site cvstart.org.
materials.k075: 2 AI interviews (persona hypotheses Sarah and Markus) and the synthetic beta funnel synthetic_funnel.csv (seed=7, 12 weeks). Flagged origin=synthetic: fine for hypotheses and method illustration — it does not prove demand.
materials.k077: CVStart — an open-source (MIT) AI resume builder and job-search dashboard, the product the agent ran its end-to-end pass on.
materials.k079: A live landing page in 19 locales: AI job scoring 0.0–5.0, CV Studio, cover letters, a tracker with follow-up. 100% local, "$0 forever", no monetization.
materials.k083: Open code under MIT: ~7,602 automated tests, 18 BYOK + keyless LLM providers, a scan of ~129 job boards, screenshots of all 19 locales in images/.
